section_summary: This section comprises documents from decimal file 894.43 covering Japanese political, cultural, patriotic, and bilateral friendship societies between 1932 and 1939 (including a 1923 retrospective report). It details the membership and nationalistic tendencies of youth and reservist associations, the establishment and platform of Kenzo Adachi's Kokumin Domei, and the founding and propaganda activities of the Society for International Cultural Relations (Kokusai Bunka Shinko Kai), including its planned New York branch at Rockefeller Center. In addition, the file records the functions and bilateral goodwill initiatives of the America-Japan Society of Tokyo, the Japan-America Society of Kwansai, the International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society, and the Philippine-Japan Society.

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet and attached extract from Tokyo Despatch No. 588 reporting on reactionary tendencies in Japanese youth organizations and national defence associations.
subfiles.summary: Extract of Despatch 588 on reactionary youth movements and national defense groups, including the Imperial Reservists Association, Young Men's Associations and Navy and Sea Defence associations.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Despatch No. 588 with Extract regarding Reactionary Tendencies in Japanese Youth and National Defence Organizations

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Despatch No. 180 concerning the Kokumin Domei formed by Kenzo Adachi.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Tokyo Despatch 180 of September 20, 1932 on the Kokumin Domei, a new party organized by Kenzo Adachi after leaving the Minseito.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Despatch No. 180 regarding Kokumin Domei

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting on the formation, platform, and policy of Kenzo Adachi's new political party, the Kokumin Domei, with enclosed translations of party documents.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports on the establishment of the Kokumin Domei (National League or People's League) led by former Home Minister Kenzo Adachi following the collapse of the Wakatsuki Cabinet. The despatch analyzes the party's influence in the Diet, where thirty Lower House members defected from the Minseito to join it, securing an absolute majority for the Seiyukai. Enclosed are English translations of the party's declaration of principles, three-point platform, and thirteen-point provisional outline of policy, which advocates state economic control, judicial independence, and a Japan-Manchukuo economic bloc.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 180: The Kokumin Domei, A New Political Organization

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Despatch No. 798 regarding the newly established Society for International Cultural Relations.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Despatch 798 of May 22, 1934 enclosing a pamphlet on the Society for International Cultural Relations under Prince Konoe.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Despatch No. 798 regarding The Society for International Cultural Relations

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting a prospectus pamphlet and press report on the inaugural diplomatic reception of the Society for International Cultural Relations (Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai).
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits literature describing the newly organized Society for International Cultural Relations (Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai), headed by Prince Fumimaro Konoe, and reports on an inaugural tea party held for the Tokyo diplomatic corps at the Peers' Club. The despatch notes that the society seeks to promote Japanese culture abroad in order to offset foreign hostility aroused by Japan's aggressive foreign policy. Enclosures include the society's published prospectus and ten-point activity program, a list of officers, an exhibition list of Suzuki Harunobu color prints from Shigekichi Mihara's collection, and a report from The Japan Advertiser featuring speeches by Marquis Yorisada Tokugawa and Belgian Ambassador Baron Albert de Bassompierre.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 798: Transmitting Pamphlets Describing the Proposed Activities of The Society for International Cultural Relations

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 1245 regarding the Kokusai Bunka Shinko Kai.
subfiles.summary: Turner summarizes Despatch 1245: the Kokusai Bunka Shinko Kai is a semi-official foundation with Foreign Office subsidy and about one million yen in contributions, chaired by Count Kabayama, unifying cultural information activities.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Tokyo Despatch No. 1245 on the Kokusai Bunka Shinko Kai

subfiles.about: Despatch analyzing the organization, finances, leadership, and cultural propaganda work of the Society for International Cultural Relations (Kokusai Bunka Shinko Kai).
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew provides a detailed report on the first year of operations of the Kokusai Bunka Shinko Kai, incorporated on April 14, 1934. He outlines its financial backing, which includes a 300,000 yen subsidy from the Japanese Foreign Office and private corporate support from Mitsui and Mitsubishi bringing total funds to around one million yen. The report discusses its leadership under Count Aisuke Kabayama and Baron Ino Dan, its public library in Marunouchi, and specific projects such as assisting American legal scholar Dr. John Henry Wigmore and hosting the Garden Club of America, advising that American scholars might utilize its resources advantageously.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1245: Society for International Cultural Relations

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum noting the Tokyo Embassy's transmittal of the new Japanese quarterly magazine NIPPON.
subfiles.summary: Turner tells Dooman Despatch 1300 sends the quarterly NIPPON, which works with the Society for International Cultural Relations, a semi-official Foreign Office-subsidized propaganda agency.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Tokyo Despatch No. 1300 and the Quarterly Magazine NIPPON

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting issue No. 3 of NIPPON, an illustrated multilingual quarterly magazine published in Tokyo for foreign distribution.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 1300: Grew sends the April 1935 NIPPON, published in four languages with modest circulation, which carries the society's activities on page 8.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1300: Sample Copy of New Quarterly, NIPPON

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet recording remarks by Marquis Tokugawa regarding the formation of a society to foster cultural ties with the Philippines.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Despatch 1363 of June 24, 1935; Marquis Tokugawa told Grew of a new society for Japan-Philippines cultural relations.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Despatch No. 1363 regarding Philippine Cultural Relations

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 2974 on Count Kabayama's mission to establish a New York branch of the Society for International Cultural Relations.
subfiles.summary: Schuler summarizes Despatch 2974: Count Kabayama will set up a New York branch of the cultural society in Rockefeller Center under Tamon Maeda and arrive in Washington around June 20.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Despatch No. 2974 and Culture Society Branch for New York

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting Count Aisuke Kabayama's voyage to the United States to establish a New York branch and library for the Society for International Cultural Relations.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 2974: Kabayama sailed to establish a New York branch and library with research facilities and exchanges, Maeda to take charge in autumn 1938; encloses a Japan Advertiser clipping.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2974: Culture Society Branch for New York

subfiles.about: State Department subject jacket establishing the file for the Japan-America Society under decimal classification 894.43.
subfiles.summary: File jacket 894.43, Japan-America Society, dated June 20, 1932, with archival preservation instructions.
subfiles.title: File Jacket: 894.43 Japan-America Society

subfiles.about: Consular despatch from Kobe reporting on the founding, officers, and aims of the Japan-America Society of Kwansai.
subfiles.summary: Consul Dickover reports the February 26, 1923 inauguration of the Japan-America Society of Kwansai under Kojiro Matsukata, formed by Japanese business leaders and American residents; American membership is selective to avoid missionary or radical influence.
subfiles.title: Despatch regarding Organization of the Japan-America Society of Kwansai

subfiles.about: Consular despatch transmitting a commemorative booklet on the official visit of Consuls Dickover and Donovan to Wakayama Prefecture.
keywords: Japan-America Society of the City of Wakayama
subfiles.summary: Despatch 19: Consul Donovan reports he and Dickover attended the December 5, 1931 inaugural meeting of the Japan-America Society of Wakayama, the first official US visit to the prefecture.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 19: Visit of Consuls Dickover and Donovan to Wakayama Prefecture, Japan

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Despatch No. 476 regarding Prince Iyesato Tokugawa's prospective visits to the United States.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Despatch 476 of July 19, 1933 on Prince Iyesato Tokugawa's travels to the US in 1933-1934 as president of the America-Japan Society.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Despatch No. 476 regarding Prince Iyesato Tokugawa's Visit to the United States

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum calling attention to Viscount Kaneko's letter setting forth his views on the 1924 Exclusion Act.
subfiles.summary: Salisbury recommends reading Viscount Kaneko's letter on the 1924 Exclusion Act, enclosed with Despatch 576.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Viscount Kaneko's Letter on the Exclusion Act

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting historical Special Bulletins of the America-Japan Society of Tokyo for preservation in the Department archives.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 576: Grew sends nine Special Bulletins of the America-Japan Society, highlighting Kaneko's letter resigning its presidency after the 1924 Immigration Act.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 576: Transmitting Special Bulletins of The America-Japan Society of Tokyo

subfiles.about: State Department instruction acknowledging receipt of Tokyo Despatch No. 576 and confirming placement of the bulletins in the Department Library.
subfiles.summary: Department acknowledges Despatch 576 of November 9, 1933 and places the Society's Special Bulletins in the State Department Library.
subfiles.title: Instruction acknowledging Despatch No. 576 on Special Bulletins of the America-Japan Society

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum evaluating the speeches published in America-Japan Society Bulletin No. 14.
subfiles.summary: Dooman comments that Despatch 884 sends Special Bulletin 14 of the America-Japan Society; Grew's speeches were already received and the others are not particularly interesting.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Despatch No. 884 and America-Japan Society Speeches

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting Special Bulletin No. 14 containing principal speeches delivered at America-Japan Society gatherings during 1933-1934.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 884: Grew sends Special Bulletin 14 (May 1934) compiling the Society's principal addresses for the year ending April 30, 1934.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 884: Transmitting Special Bulletins of The America-Japan Society of Tokyo

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet regarding a proposed dinner by the America-Japan Society for the visiting U.S. Congressional delegation.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Takashi Komatsu's letter on the America-Japan Society's wish to host a dinner or luncheon for the Vice President and visiting Congressional delegation (033.1111b Congressional Delegation/38).
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Letter regarding Proposed Dinner for U.S. Congressional Delegation

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 3542 and luncheon speeches by General Burnett and Admiral Nomura.
subfiles.summary: Memo on Despatch 3542: speeches by General Burnett and Admiral Nomura at the December 12, 1938 America-Japan Society luncheon express familiar sentiments and need not be read.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Despatch No. 3542 and Speeches of General Burnett and Admiral Nomura

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting a press report of speeches delivered by General Charles Burnett, Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura, and Count Aisuke Kabayama at the America-Japan Society.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 3542: at the December 12, 1938 luncheon for General Burnett, Nomura compared Japan's China aims to the Monroe Doctrine and said Japanese diplomacy cries too much; Burnett praised Japan's courage; Kabayama reviewed Burnett's earthquake relief.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3542: Speech of Brigadier-General Charles Burnett at America-Japan Society, December 12, 1938

subfiles.about: State Department subject jacket establishing the file for the International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society of Tokyo under decimal classification 894.43.
keywords: International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society of Tokyo
subfiles.summary: File jacket 894.43 KOI-NOBORI, International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society of Tokyo, dated April 22, 1935.
subfiles.title: File Jacket: 894.43 The International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society of Tokyo

subfiles.about: Letter from the Boy Scouts of America inquiring about the International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society of Tokyo, transmitting an enclosed appeal from Soichi Saito.
keywords: International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society of Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Boy Scouts of America asks whether to cooperate with the Tokyo society that sent koi-nobori carp flags as goodwill tokens, to be displayed in a park, YMCA or store.
subfiles.title: Letter from Boy Scouts of America regarding International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society

subfiles.about: State Department letter providing biographical information on Soichi Saito, signatory of the International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton says the Department lacks information on the society but its signer Soichi Saito is Secretary General of Japan's YMCA federation and an Institute of Pacific Relations delegate.
subfiles.title: Letter to Boy Scouts of America regarding the International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society

subfiles.about: Letter from the Boy Scouts of America expressing appreciation for State Department information on Soichi Saito, accompanied by Scouting literature.
subfiles.summary: E. H. Vitalius of the Boy Scouts of America thanks Maxwell M. Hamilton for providing biographical background on Soichi Saito and the International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society. Accompaniments to the letter include promotional leaflets and order forms detailing Boy Scouts of America handicraft publications and official patrol leader handbooks.
subfiles.title: Letter from Boy Scouts of America acknowledging Information on Soichi Saito (with Attachments)

subfiles.about: State Department subject jacket establishing the file for the Philippine-Japan Society under decimal classification 894.43.
subfiles.summary: File jacket 894.43 for the Philippine-Japan Society, inaugurated to promote cultural relations, dated September 5, 1935.
subfiles.title: File Jacket: 894.43 Philippine-Japan Society

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum analyzing the diplomatic significance of the newly established Philippine-Japan Society.
subfiles.summary: Turner tells Dooman the Embassy sees the Philippine-Japan Society's founding as reflecting Japanese interest stimulated by the coming Philippine Commonwealth.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Tokyo Despatch No. 1457 on Formation of the Philippine-Japan Society

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting the inauguration of the Philippine-Japan Society under Marquis Yorisada Tokugawa, transmitting an enclosed newspaper report.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 1457: the Philippine-Japan Society was founded at Tokyo August 23, 1935 under Marquis Yorisada Tokugawa, reflecting Japanese interest in the Philippines before the transition; enclosed Tokyo Nichi Nichi account names officers and Philippine backers.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1457: Philippine-Japan Society Created at Tokyo

subfiles.about: State Department subject jacket establishing the file for the Shiunso under decimal classification 894.43.
subfiles.summary: File jacket 894.43 SHIUNSO, 'A Society in Japan', dated July 7, 1932.
subfiles.title: File Jacket: 894.43 The Shiunso

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Despatch No. 43 regarding an open letter from the reactionary Shiunso to the Lytton Commission.

subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Despatch 43 of July 7, 1932, an open letter from the small reactionary Shiunso to the Lytton Commission restating Japan's China and Manchuria policy.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Despatch No. 43 regarding Open Letter from the Shiunso

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum recommending an article by the Japanese Foreign Minister containing recollections of the late diplomat Enjiro Yamaza.
subfiles.summary: Dooman recommends Despatch 619's translation of Foreign Minister Hirota's article on diplomat Enjiro Yamaza for insight into Hirota's background and character.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Despatch No. 619 and Foreign Minister's Recollections of Diplomat Yamaza
